In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present structure of Plasiodium falciparump triose-phosphate-isomerase-2-phosphoglyerate complex is the most detailed description of an active site of a triose-phosphate- isomerase to date.

2-phospho-glycerate does not bind to the enzyme in a manner that mimics the transition state, but it is a potent inhibitor that binds in two orientations and induces conformational changes in the active-site loop and in certain residues that flank the loop.
the active site geometry of P. falciparum is very similar to that of S. cerevisiae, and the active site of L. mexicana is similar to that of the S. cerevisiaee and P. falciparium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the catalytic loop 5 and loop 6 are the two major elements of conformational flexibility in the enzyme.
the active-site residues are highly conserved, but the loop 6 and the surrounding residues are more flexible in the Plasmodium enzyme.
the catalytic mechanism of triose-phosphate Isomerases is highly conserved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2-phospho-glycerate, which has a similar chemical structure as the transition-state analogue 1-phosphogly-colate, is not a good mimic of the transition state.
2-phospho-glycerate is a potent inhibitor of Plasmodial triose-phosphate Isomerases.
the active site of P. falciparum isomerase has a large capacity to accommodate different ligands and that the enzyme has the capability of binding two different ligands in the same active site.
